About.description: `GET /api/bmc/about` -- what this board and this daemon are.

api.description: The `/api/bmc` contract version, not a release of anything.

board_model.description:
From the board's EEPROM. Empty on a board that cannot be read, rather
than absent: upstream's shape, and the interface renders the blank.

board_serial.description: `None` when the EEPROM field is missing or blank after trimming.

build_version.description:
The same value as `bmcd_version`. The web interface reads this key for
its "Build version" field and renders `vundefined` without it, so it
is duplicated deliberately rather than left for the client to alias.

kernel.description:
The running kernel. `"unknown"` when `uname` cannot be read; the one
field an operator wants after a kernel bump.

version.description:
The firmware, from `/etc/os-release`. `"unknown"` when it cannot be
read -- a string, because an About page with a gap is still worth
rendering and this field has never been nullable.

BoardInfo.description:
`GET /api/bmc/info` -- what the Overview page reads.

Both halves are already typed elsewhere; this names the object that wraps
them so the document has one schema rather than an inline shape.

file.description: For a local candidate, the file it came from.

age_seconds.description:
How old these answers are. A caller that needs to say "as of a minute
ago" should not have to parse `checked_at` and trust two clocks.

refreshing.description:
These are the previous answers and a refresh is running behind them.

The page draws a spinner on its "check now" control and leaves the
list underneath readable, rather than blanking or freezing. Skipped
when false so a settled catalogue serialises as it always did.

ChannelState.description: What one channel resolves to, straight from `tpi-selfupdate --json`.

Clock.description: Whether the board knows what time it is, and how well.

measured_by.description:
How the three fields above were obtained, because it is not a file
read like everything else here.

offset_seconds.description: System clock minus true time: negative when the board is behind.

rtc.description:
Every RTC the kernel has. An empty list is a board with none, which
is a board whose clock starts at the epoch on every cold boot.

source.description: What it is synchronised to, as chrony names it.

synchronised.description:
Whether the system clock is disciplined. `null` when chrony's state
could not be read at all.

exported_at.description:
When and from what. Not read back on import; it is what makes a file
found on a workstation six months later identifiable.

Cooler.description:
One cooling device: something the thermal framework can turn up, in whole
steps, to cool a zone. On this board that is the fan.

This is deliberately not [`crate::app::cooling_device::CoolingDevice`],
which is the shape `opt=get&type=cooling` has served for years and which
the fan control in the web UI writes back to. That one renames `pwm-fan`
to the platform node behind it and reports the raw steps as `speed` and
`max_speed`. This one passes the kernel's own names and numbers through.

cur_state.description:
Which step the device is on right now. Steps are an index, not a
percentage and not an RPM: `4` of `6` is the fifth of seven settings.

levels.description:
What each step does, indexed by step: `levels[cur_state]` is the PWM
duty the fan is being driven at, out of the 255 the pwm-fan binding
counts in. Read out of the board's own device tree, so it is a fact
about this board and not a table copied into a client. `None` on a
board that does not describe one, which is not the same as a fan that
runs flat out -- see [`cooling_levels`].

max_level.description:
The duty at `max_state`, which is the last entry of `levels`: the
denominator for turning a step into a percentage. 254 here, not 255 --
this board's top step is not quite full duty, and saying 255 would be
inventing the difference.

name.description:
The device's `type`, as the driver spells it: `pwm-fan`. Falls back to
the directory name.

overridden.description:
Whether that zone's governor is paused, which is the only condition
under which a step written here is a step that holds.

With the governor running, `step_wise` returns the fan to the trip the
board is above within a poll, so a written step is a request the
kernel is about to overrule. Reported so a client can say which of
those two things is happening, rather than leaving a person to watch a
slider spring back and draw their own conclusion.

zone.description:
The thermal zone whose governor drives this device, when one binds it.

A zone binds a cooling device once per trip it should react to, so
this board's single fan is `cdev0` through `cdev3` of the one zone.
Every one of those links is the same answer.

FirmwareSlots.description: The A/B slot state of the board.

last_promotion.description: The last line the promotion script wrote, when there is a log.

nextboot.description:
The raw `nextboot` variable when it is set, so a caller can see what
is staged and not merely that something is.

present.description:
Whether the UBI device is there at all. False on a board that boots
from something else, and on any kernel without UBI: the rest of the
fields are then empty because there is nothing to read, not because
something failed.

promotion_history.description:
How the gate has decided over this board's life. `None` on a board
with no log, which is a board that has never taken an OTA update.

rollback.description:
The slot a rollback would land on, when one can be named without
guessing.

running.description:
The slot the board booted from, identified by which volume has an
attached `ubiblock` device.

staged.description:
Which image is staged, when whatever staged it left a note. `None`
means no note was found -- on a board where `update_staged` is true
that means the image was staged by something that does not write one,
not that nothing is staged.

update_staged.description:
Whether an update is staged for the next boot. `null` means the
U-Boot environment could not be read at all -- no `fw_printenv` on the
board -- which is not the same as "no update is staged".

uptime_seconds.description:
Seconds since the BMC booted, as `/proc/uptime` gives it. Not the
uptime of any compute module.

Hostname.description:
`GET /api/bmc/hostname` -- live, and after the next boot.

The two differ between a rename and the reboot that settles it, which is
the whole reason both are reported.

hostname.description: What `sethostname(2)` currently says. `None` if it cannot be read.

on_next_boot.description: What `/etc/hostname` holds. `None` when the file is absent.

Load.description: The one-, five- and fifteen-minute load averages.

Memory.description:
Memory, in bytes rather than the kibibytes `/proc/meminfo` speaks.

This is not an academic number on this board. It has 116 MB in total, and
a firmware image being uploaded into `/tmp` is competing with the daemon
for it.

available_bytes.description:
`MemAvailable`: what a new allocation can actually get, reclaim
included. Absent on kernels older than 3.14, which is why it is not
derived from the other two.

self_resident_bytes.description:
This daemon's own resident set, from `/proc/self/statm`.

Board-level memory says the board is being consumed; it cannot say by
what. On 2026-09-09 the board wedged after losing 1 MB a minute under
polling and the metrics could only show the total falling, so the
diagnosis had to be argued from timing rather than read off
(SQU-172). One number closes that gap.

self_threads.description:
How many threads this daemon has, from `/proc/self/status`.

The companion to the resident set, and the one that says *which kind*
of growth is happening. A heap leak grows the resident set with a flat
thread count; a leaked task or an unreaped blocking thread grows both
together, because every thread carries a stack.

Without it the two are indistinguishable from the outside, which is
the position SQU-172 left us in: memory falling about a megabyte a
minute with no way to say whether it was allocations or threads.

Nand.description: What is left of the NAND, as UBI counts it.

available_bytes.description:
`available_eraseblocks` in bytes, for callers that would otherwise
multiply the two themselves.

available_eraseblocks.description:
Logical eraseblocks not yet handed to a volume. This is the number
that says whether the next firmware upgrade has room.

bad_eraseblocks.description: Physical eraseblocks the flash has retired.

present.description: Whether the UBI device is there at all.

reserved_eraseblocks.description:
Physical eraseblocks held back to replace bad ones. When this reaches
zero the next bad block is a failure rather than a substitution.

NodePower.description:
`GET /api/bmc/power` -- one element, four nodes.

Each value is a **string**, not a boolean: `"0"`, `"1"`, or `"Unknown"`
when the daemon could not read the rail. Upstream's shape; a client that
wants a boolean has to handle the third case anyway.

Ntp.description: `GET /api/bmc/ntp` -- the time sources, and how the clock is doing.

configurable.description:
False on an image whose `chrony.conf` predates the `sourcedir` line.
Without it a saved list is written and silently never read, so the
interface must be able to say the setting does nothing.

PortKind.description: What sits on the other side of a switch port.

Problem.description: RFC 9457. `detail` is the same message the legacy form puts in `result`.

Promotion.description: What the promotion script last said it did.

message.description:
Everything the script said after its marker. Not classified into
success or failure here, because the vocabulary of that log belongs to
the firmware and not to this daemon.

timestamp.description:
The date the script itself printed, passed through verbatim rather
than reformatted: it is the board's own idea of the time, which on a
BMC that has just come up may be well before the real one.

PromotionHistory.description:
How the health gate has decided, over the life of this board.

The gate's history lived only in `/mnt/overlay/postupdate.log`, so
"nineteen consecutive clean promotions" was a number somebody counted by
hand and wrote on a website, where it went stale the next day.

attempts.description: Boots that ran the gate at all: one per "tentative boot" line.

promoted.description:
The rest. Derived rather than counted, because the gate has no single
line that means "kept": it can finish through the metrics check, or by
skipping it on a board with no `curl`, or by promoting anyway when
there is no volume to fall back to. Deriving covers all three; the one
inaccuracy is a board cut mid-gate, whose unfinished attempt counts
here. That is rare and errs towards over-reporting success, which is
worth saying out loud in the metric's help text.

rolled_back.description: Of those, the ones the gate refused.

Relation.description:
How a candidate relates to what is running.

`Unknown` is not a failure. A board built from a working tree reports
`VERSION=local`, and ordering that against real tags is meaningless --
measured on hardware, `sort -V` put `local` first and every release,
including genuinely older code, came out as an upgrade. Saying "unknown" is
the honest answer and lets the page say so rather than implying an order.

Rtc.description: One real-time clock the kernel has.

name.description:
The driver's own name for it. Which of the two has a battery behind
it is not something the kernel exposes, so it is not claimed here.

SdCard.description: `GET /api/bmc/sdcard` -- bytes, from `statvfs` on the mount point.

use.description:
Named `use`, not `used`. Upstream's spelling, and a Rust keyword,
which is why the field is renamed rather than called what it means.

directory.description:
`true` for a directory, so a client can render a tree without a second
request per row.

flashable.description: Whether this could be written to a compute module.

modified.description: Seconds since the epoch, or `None` where the filesystem will not say.

path.description:
Path relative to the card's root, which is also what a later request
sends back. Never absolute: the root is the daemon's to decide.

reason.description:
Why not, when it is not. Present ONLY alongside `flashable: false`.

A non-candidate is listed rather than hidden: an operator who cannot
find the file they just copied will not conclude "it must be too
small", they will conclude the page is broken.

size.description:
Bytes. Meaningless for a directory and reported as 0 rather than
omitted, because an absent field and a zero are the same thing to most
clients and only one of them is true.

size_bytes.description:
`data_bytes` of the volume: how much firmware is in it, not how much
space it was given.

version.description:
Firmware version, and only ever for the running slot. The rollback
volume is not mounted -- nothing on this board reads a squashfs that
is not the root filesystem -- so its `/etc/os-release` is not
reachable, and a version is not guessed from a volume name.

volume.description: UBI volume name, as the volume itself spells it.

volume_id.description: Volume id within the UBI device, the `N` of `ubi0_N`.

id.description:
Stable identifier, used by the install call. Not the label: renaming a
source in the interface must not change what an install refers to.

location.description: `owner/repo` for github, a URL prefix for http, a path for local.

error.description:
Why this source produced nothing, when it produced nothing for a
reason. An empty list with no error means the source genuinely offers
nothing; an empty list WITH an error means it could not be read. The
page must not collapse those two into "up to date".

SourceKind.description: Where a source's images come from.

oneOf.description: A GitHub repository, `owner/repo`. Checksums are published and checked.

An HTTP directory of `<prefix>/<version>/<image>.tpu`. Checksums are
used when the publisher ships them; upstream's does not.

A directory on the SD card. This is also where uploads land, so an
uploaded image becomes a candidate like any other.

StagedImage.description:
What is waiting in the staging volume, according to whatever put it there.

Every field is optional because this file is written by something else --
`tpi-selfupdate`, or the daemon's own upgrade worker -- and a marker from
an older writer should degrade to "less is known", never to no answer.

file.description:
The file it came from, when the stager knew a name but not a tag --
an uploaded image whose filename does not follow the release naming
has a file and no version, and saying so beats inventing a version.

sha256.description:
The checksum the stager verified before writing the volume, so a
caller can tell two builds of one tag apart.

source.description:
What staged it -- `tpi-selfupdate`, `upload`. Useful when a board has
a staged image nobody remembers arming.

staged_at.description: When it was staged, in the board's own idea of the time.

version.description: The release tag, as the stager spelled it: `v2.4.0`.

SwitchPort.description:
One port of the switch. Every field the kernel would not give us is
`None` rather than a stand-in value: a port that is down has no speed and
no duplex, and saying `0` there would read as a working port running at
nothing.

duplex.description:
`full` or `half`. The kernel reports `unknown` for a port with no
link, which becomes `None` here.

link.description: `carrier`: a peer is electrically there and has trained.

name.description: Interface name, as the kernel spells it.

operstate.description:
`operstate`: `up`, `down`, `lowerlayerdown`, `unknown`. Passed through
verbatim, because the distinction between `down` (nobody asked for the
port) and `lowerlayerdown` (asked for, nothing on the wire) is the
whole point of reading it.

present.description:
Whether the kernel has a netdev for this port at all. False means the
switch driver did not register it -- on a board where the driver fails
to probe, all six read false while the BMC itself stays reachable over
its own interface.

speed_mbps.description:
Megabit per second. The kernel reports `-1` for a port with no link,
which becomes `None` here.

ThermalSensor.description: One thermal zone: a sensor the kernel can read a temperature from.

name.description:
The zone's `type`, which is the name its driver registered -- ours is
`bmc-thermal`, from the device tree node. Falls back to the directory
name if the kernel will not answer, so a sensor is never nameless.

present.description:
Whether a temperature was actually read. False is "the zone exists and
the kernel would not tell us", which is not the same as a reading of
zero, and not the same as the zone not existing -- a zone that does not
exist is not in the list at all.

temperature_c.description:
Degrees Celsius to one decimal, converted from the millidegrees sysfs
reports. `None` when the zone is there but would not give a reading.

trips.description:
The zone's trip points, in the order the kernel numbers them.

This is what makes the fan's step explicable rather than mysterious.
The governor is `step_wise`, so the step is a consequence of which
trips the board has crossed -- and "the fan is on step 4" with no
reason attached is the question this fork was asked to investigate.
Read from sysfs for the same reason as the cooling levels: it is a
fact about this board, not a table copied into a client.

Trip.description: One trip point: a temperature and what crossing it means.

index.description: The kernel's index for it, which is also its order.

kind.description:
`active` drives a cooling device; `hot` and `critical` are the
kernel's own escalations. Passed through as the kernel spells it
rather than mapped, because a client that meets an unfamiliar type
should show it, not swallow it.

Trust.description:
How much is known about an image's integrity.

Three genuinely different things that a page must not render alike: a
checksum published by the release and verified on download; TLS only,
because the publisher ships no checksums at all (upstream's server does
not); and a local file whose provenance is whatever put it there.

checked_at.description: When this was last resolved, in the board's own idea of the time.

edge.description: The edge channel: the newest release including pre-releases.

error.description:
Why a channel is missing, when one is. Present WITH a channel too,
when only one of the two could be resolved.

stable.description: The stable channel: what GitHub marks Latest, pre-releases excluded.

UsbState.description: `GET /api/bmc/usb` -- which node holds the bus, in which mode.

bus_type.description: What the hardware is: which of the board's USB controllers is in play.

node.description: The node, as a display string such as `Node 1`.

route.description: Where the bus is routed: the alternative port, the BMC, or a node.

basic.description: The board's root credentials. Loopback on the board itself needs neither.

info.description: The board management controller of a Turing Pi 2, as built by the excavador-turing fork. Every operation here is also reachable in the legacy form `GET /api/bmc?opt=&type=`, which older clients speak and which is not going away.
